name: Griddled Beef & Esquites Meal Prep Bowls
description: Hearty meal prep bowls featuring seasoned griddled beef, roasted sweet potatoes, and thinned refried beans, all topped with a creamy, charred corn esquites mixture.

ingredients.name: Beef broth, water, or bacon grease
Jalapeños
ingredients.notes: Finely diced, seeds removed for less heat

instructions: 1. Roast the Sweet Potatoes: Preheat the oven to 425°F. Toss the diced sweet potatoes in a large bowl with neutral oil, salt, and pepper. Divide them evenly across 3-4 large rimmed baking sheets, ensuring they are spread out in a single layer. Bake for 25-30 minutes, rotating the pans halfway through, until deeply caramelized and tender.

2. Prep the Refried Beans: Place a heavy Dutch oven (like a Le Creuset) on the stove over medium-low heat. Add all the refried beans along with a splash of broth, water, or bacon grease. Stir continuously until heated through and smoothed out. The goal is a creamy, slightly loosened consistency. Keep warm.

3. Emulsify the Binder: Load the avocados, mayonnaise, crema, lime juice, salt, and a generous shake of Tajín into a Vitamix or high-powered blender. Blend on medium-high until completely smooth and vibrant green.

4. Fire Up the Griddle: Get a 36-inch griddle screaming hot and set up two cooking zones. THE VEGGIE ZONE (High Heat): Lay down a thin coat of oil and drop the dried corn. Let it sit untouched for a minute or two to develop a hard, dark char. Once blistered, toss it with the diced jalapeños and serranos just long enough to take the raw bite out of the peppers. Remove and let cool.

5. The Meat Zone: THE MEAT ZONE (Medium-High Heat): Drop the 8 pounds of beef. Work it across the surface, chopping and browning. Once cooked through, fold in the taco seasoning and splash a little water across the meat to hydrate the spices and coat the beef evenly. Remove from the heat.
6. Mix the Esquites: In a massive mixing bowl, fold the cooled, charred corn and pepper mix together with the blended avocado-crema and the crumbled cotija cheese until fully combined.

7. Assemble the Containers: Line up 16 meal prep containers and build in this specific order: Layer 1 (The Smear): Spread a layer of the thinned, warm refried beans directly onto the bottom. Layer 2 (The Bulk): Drop in an even portion of the roasted sweet potatoes. Layer 3 (The Protein): Portion exactly 0.5 lbs of the seasoned griddled beef onto the potatoes. Layer 4 (The Cap): Top the beef with a thick, generous scoop of the wet esquites mixture to seal everything in. Allow to cool slightly before capping with lids.
cookNotes: Yields 16 servings with 0.5 lbs of protein per serving.
The avocado-crema binder acts as a sealant to keep the beef moist.
Dried corn is essential for a proper char on the griddle; do not skip drying it.
Serve with tortilla chips for crunch.
